"''Wherever I go, he goes.''"
"''So I've heard.|Gor Koresh and Din Djarin|}} '''Gor Koresh''' was an [[Abyssin]] [[gangster]], [[gambler]], and entrepreneur who [[Homeworld|hailed]] from the [[planet]] [[RTK111]]. He organized [[gladiator]] matches at his arena—[[Gor Koresh's Honky Tonk]]—on RTK111 and [[Hunting|hunted]] [[Mandalorian]] remnants for their [[beskar]] [[Mandalorian armor|armor]] during the [[New Republic]]'s [[New Republic Era|reign]]. At his arena in [[9 ABY]], the Abyssin met the Mandalorian [[bounty hunter]] [[Din Djarin]] and the [[Youngling|infant]] [[Din Grogu|Grogu]]. The Mandalorian inquired about finding others of his kind, but Koresh advised the [[bounty]] hunter to enjoy the entertainment first. Koresh attempted to trick the Mandalorian into a bet in order to win the bounty hunter's beskar [[Din Djarin's armor|armor]], but when Djarin refused the offer, the Abyssin and his assailants held the bounty hunter at [[Blaster|gunpoint]]. Nevertheless, Djarin defeated Koresh's allies and intercepted Koresh outside the fighting pit, interrogating the Abyssin for the information he desired. After Koresh gave in, the Mandalorian left him to face [[wild dog]]s. ==Biography== ===Ringside negotiations=== {{Quote|Well, I'll bet you the information you seek that this Gamorrean's going to die within the next minute and a half. And all you have to put up in exchange is your shiny beskar armor.''"
"''I'm prepared to pay you for the information. I'm not leaving my fate up to chance.|Koresh and Djarin|}} The [[Abyssin]] Gor Koresh lived during the [[New Republic Era|reign]] of the [[New Republic]], [[Homeworld|hailing]] from the [[planet]] [[RTK111]]. As a [[gangster]], [[gambler]],{{Databank|gor-koresh|Gor Koresh}} informant,{{EncyclopediaCite|Post-Galactic Civil War and the Mandalorian}} and entrepreneur,{{InsiderCite|210|Mandalorian Mayhem}} Gor Koresh profited from various criminal activities, including organizing underworld [[gladiator]] matches at his own arena, [[Gor Koresh's Honky Tonk]], in the [[Warehouse district (Carnita arena)|warehouse district]][[The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian (Season Two)|''The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian'' Season Two]] of a barren [[city]] on RTK111. He also hunted [[Mandalorian]] remnants for their [[Mandalorian armor|armor]] made of [[beskar]], which was rising in value. Koresh at some point heard about a supposed Mandalorian on the [[planet]] [[Tatooine]]. The apparent Mandalorian was in reality [[Cobb Vanth]], the [[marshal]] of the Tatooine [[mining]] town [[Freetown|Mos Pelgo]] who had acquired a set of [[Boba Fett's armor|Mandalorian armor]] from [[Jawa]]s in [[4 ABY]].[[Cobb Vanth]] acquires [[Boba Fett's armor|Mandalorian armor]] during the events of [[Aftermath (novel)|''Aftermath'']], which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of to [[4 ABY]]. Koresh also learned about the Mandalorian [[bounty hunter]] [[Din Djarin]], who closely protected the [[Youngling|infant]] [[foundling]] [[Din Grogu|Grogu]]. [[File:Koresh-negotiates-CH9.png|thumb|left|350px|Gor Koresh speaks to Din Djarin at his arena.]] In [[9 ABY]],{{MandoDate|9}} Djarin traveled to Koresh's arena, having been told that the gangster knew of the whereabouts of other Mandalorians. Koresh sat ringside at his arena, betting on [[Unidentified Gamorrean fighter 2|one]] of the [[Gamorrean]] fighters in the ring, when he was approached by Djarin and Grogu. Looking between the pair, the gambler remarked that the pit was no place for a child like Grogu, but the Mandalorian stated that the foundling went wherever he went. Djarin told Koresh that he was looking for information on other Mandalorians in [[the galaxy]] as part of a quest to return Grogu to his own [[Jedi|kind]]. Koresh, more fixated on the fight, advised the [[bounty]] hunter to enjoy the entertainment instead of going straight to business. The Gamorrean that Koresh had bet on was knocked to the ground, so the displeased gangster shouted for the [[Unidentified Gamorrean fighter 1|other Gamorrean]] to [[Death|kill]] their opponent. As the injured Gamorrean struggled to survive, Koresh put the information Djarin needed up for a bet on whether the losing Gamorrean would die within the next [[Standard minute|minute]] and a half. In turn, the Abyssin requested the Mandalorian put up his beskar [[Din Djarin's armor|armor]] for the bet, willing to trade information about other Mandalorians in exchange for the set. Djarin refused and instead offered to pay for the knowledge instead so Koresh shot the winning Gamorrean with his [[blaster pistol]], and his armed assailants swiftly surrounded the Mandalorian with their own [[blaster]]s drawn as part of Koresh's own trap. ===Unsuccessful hunt=== {{Quote|Beskar's value continues to rise. I've grown quite fond of it. Give it to me now or I will peel it off your corpse.''"
"''Tell me where the Mandalorians are and I'll walk outta here without killing you.|Koresh and Djarin|}} [[File:MandoKoreshWhistlingBirds-TMCh9.png|thumb|right|350px|Din Djarin releases whistling birds on Gor Koresh's armed thugs.]] The arena's audience promptly fled the venue, and Koresh bragged about not having to seek out Djarin for his [[armor]] and told his new captive of how fond he had become of the increasingly expensive beskar. The gangster demanded Djarin's armor in return for not killing the Mandalorian, but in reply, Djarin threatened to kill Koresh if he did not tell him where other Mandalorians could be found. After Koresh remarked that he thought Djarin was not a gambler, the Mandalorian used his [[whistling bird]]s to eliminate the Abyssin's armed assailants and fought the arena's workers. Koresh fled the arena as Djarin defeated the remainder of the gambler's people. Koresh ran outside and down the street when Djarin, exiting the arena, snared the gangster with his [[fibercord whip]], pulling him across the ground and hanging him on a lamppost. Turning to try and befriend his captor, the Abyssin panically offered Djarin the information he desired in return for his life, not wanting to be left as a snack for local wildlife. He revealed what he knew of the alleged Mandalorian on Tatooine, swearing the information to be true by a [[gotra]]. Djarin then began leaving, and Koresh begged to be freed from the grappling line, claiming it was part of their deal. The Mandalorian instead shot out the light post with his [[The Mandalorian's IB-94 blaster pistol|blaster pistol]], allowing several local [[wild dog]]s to advance on the gangster and try to kill him as he screamed in fear. ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|It's uncouth to talk business immediately. Just enjoy the entertainment.|Koresh, to Djarin|}} Gor Koresh was a 1.73-[[meter]]-tall (5 [[Foot|feet]], 8 inches) Abyssin with [[Color|green]] skin; gray, thinning [[hair]]; and a single brown [[eye]]. The deceitful entrepreneur had a habit of double-crossing or killing anyone who interfered with his exploits. To protect his operation, Koresh required that visitors to his arena have either his invitation or a password. He grew fond of beskar as it rose in value and hunted Mandalorians to harvest their beskar armor. The Abyssin watched Grogu come to his arena with bemusement and disapproval, believing it was no place for the child. [[File:DontLeaveMeHangin-TMCh9.png|thumb|left|350px|Fearing for his life, Gor Koresh gave up information to Din Djarin.]] Koresh tried to convince Djarin into betting for information in an attempt to trick him into handing over his beskar armor. When Djarin did not play into the gambler's trick, Koresh and his assailants held the bounty hunter at gunpoint, with Koresh chuckling as he bragged to the Mandalorian. After Djarin defeated all of Koresh's allies and apprehended him, the Abyssin gave up information on a possible Mandalorian in an attempt to preserve his life, his voice cracking as he attempted to maintain some composure while being hung from a lamppost. Koresh's voice grew hoarse and breathless as he swore his information by a gotra. ==Equipment== {{Quote|Normally, I have to seek out remnants of you Mandalorians in your hidden hives to harvest your precious shiny shells.|Koresh, to Djarin|}} Gor Koresh wore brown under-[[clothing]], brown [[glove]]s, and a white sport coat. The coat included a symbol of his arena, intended to give an air of respectability. He donned black trousers and brown [[boot]]s. He also wielded a blaster [[pistol]] that was modified for Abyssin vision. ==Behind the scenes== ===Identity=== {{Quote|Doug [Chiang] described Gor Koresh as being like an emperor of the Colosseum who gets to decide the fates of the Gamorreans.|Brian Matyas|}} [[File:Mando-Koresh-Concept-Art.jpg|thumb|right|350px|Concept art of Din Djarin and Gor Koresh by Khang Le]] Gor Koresh first appeared in "[[Chapter 9: The Marshal]]," the premiere episode of the [[The Mandalorian Season Two|second season]] of the [[Disney+]] live-action series ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'', which was directed by show-runner [[Jon Favreau]] and aired on [[October 30]], [[2020]].{{InsiderCite|202|Star Wars: The Mandalorian Season Two Companion|''Star Wars: The Mandalorian'' Season Two Companion}} Koresh was voiced by [[John Leguizamo]] and portrayed in costume by [[John Rosengrant]]. Koresh was initially teased in the official trailer for ''The Mandalorian'' Season Two, which was published on [[Wikipedia:YouTube|YouTube]] on [[September 15]], 2020.{{SWYouTube|eW7Twd85m2g|The Mandalorian | Season 2 Official Trailer | Disney+|sw_url=video/the-mandalorian-season-2-official-trailer}} On YouTube, the trailer's captions initially identified the character as "Gore Keresh,"[[:File:Gore-name-reveal.jpg|Initial YouTube captions]] but they were later changed to remove the name and simply identify the character as an [[alien]].[[:File:Gore-name-removed.jpg|Later YouTube captions]] The subtitles on the Disney+ version of the trailer wrote the name as "Gor Koresh" but were also subsequently removed.[[:File:Gor-Koresh-caption.png|Initial Disney+ captions]] The "[[Launchpad]]" section of the [[Star Wars Insider 202|202th issue]] of [[Titan Magazines]]' ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'',{{InsiderCite|202|Launchpad}} published on [[April 27]] of [[2021]],{{TitanComics|url=m/72-star-wars-insider-202|text=Star Wars Insider #202}} used the spelling "Gor Keresh," as did the "[[Jedi Master's Quiz]]" section of ''Star Wars Insider''{{'s}} [[Star Wars Insider 203|203rd issue]],{{InsiderCite|203|Jedi Master's Quiz}} published on [[June 22]] of that year.{{TitanComics|url=m/76-star-wars-insider-203|text=Star Wars Insider #203}} ===Conception and portrayal=== {{Quote|But I like you being the high status mob boss, even if you don't do the character of Don Corleone.|Jon Favreau advises John Leguizamo for voicing Gor Koresh|{{DisneyGallery|Disney Gallery: The Mandalorian: Making of Season Two|Making of Season Two}}}} In the first drafts for "Chapter 9: The Marshal," written by Favreau during the holiday break at the end of [[2018]], Koresh was described as a "foul cyclops" with a pair of [[Piercing|earrings]] and a nose ring. The director also put across the idea that the character would be sat among a crowd of spectators on simple bench seating with bodyguards rather than being a distant spectator or on a throne, while arts director [[Doug Chiang]] described Koresh to concept artists as akin to an emperor of the [[Wikipedia:Colosseum|Colosseum]], stating that he would decide the fates of competing Gamorreans. Working off of another description of Koresh as a "low-level crime boss," artist [[Brian Matyas]] gave the character a design inspired by the "old-school" work of animator{{WebCite|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/05/08/movies/ray-harryhausen-cinematic-special-effects-innovator-dies-at-92.html|text=Ray Harryhausen, Whose Creatures Battled Jason and Sinbad, Dies at 92|author=[https://www.nytimes.com/by/patrick-j-lyons Lyons, Patrick J.]|date=2013-05-07|work=[[Wikipedia:The New York Times|The New York Times]]|quote=Ray Harryhausen, the animator and special-effects wizard who found ways to breathe cinematic life into the gargantuan, the mythical and the extinct, died on Tuesday in London.|archivedate=20220709210835}} [[Wikipedia:Ray Harryhausen|Ray Harryhausen]] with a retro-style color palette. [[File:Koresh-on-set.png|thumb|left|350px|John Rosengrant as Gor Koresh on the set of the arena with Jon Favreau]] In another concept, Matyas worked off of Chiang's emperor idea, giving Koresh a very simple costume. One of Matyas's other concepts for the character included a helmet with a [[monocle]] visor, playing off of the idea of an Abyssin "[[assassin]]-hitman-henchman with a [[helmet]]." Matyas chose to make later designs resemble a classic mob boss, being inspired by [[Wikipedia:Tony Soprano|Tony Soprano]], a character from the television series [[Wikipedia:The Sopranos|''The Sopranos'']],{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/news/2007/04/sopranos200704?currentPage=1|text=An American Family|author=[[Wikipedia:Peter Biskind|Peter Biskind]]|date=2007-04-04|work=[[Wikipedia:Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]|archivedate=20120717063911}} which translated into the final design of Koresh. Some other concept art including Koresh was drawn by artist [[Khang Le]].{{SW|url=news/mando-download-chapter-9-the-marshal|text=Mando Download: "Chapter 9: The Marshal"}} During Leguizamo's rehearsal for Koresh voice, Favreau advised the voice actor to come across as a "high status mob boss" like [[Wikipedia:Don Corleone|Don Corleone]], a character from [[Wikipedia:The Godfather (film series)|''The Godfather'' film series]].{{WebCite|url=https://www.nytimes.com/movies/movie/20076/The-Godfather/cast|text=The Godfather (1972)|date=2014-04-18|work=[[Wikipedia:The New York Times|The New York Times]]|archivedate=20140418100447|nolive=1}} Lines about Koresh calling his Gamorrean the best in his stable were included during the rehearsal but did not make it into the episode. Filming for "Chapter 9: The Marshal," including Koresh's scenes, took place over thirteen days during [[November]] [[2019]].[[The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian (Season Two)|''The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian'' Season Two]] states that {{TheMandalorian|Chapter 9: The Marshal}} was filmed over thirteen days and [[Disney+]] was launched halfway through that period. Since {{SW|url=news/alan-tudyk-to-return-as-k-2so-in-cassian-andor-live-action-series|text=Alan Tudyk to Return as K-2SO in Cassian Andor Live-Action Series|nolive=1}} establishes that Disney+ launched on [[November 12]], [[2019]], the filming must have therefore taken place in [[November]] of that year. ===Novelization differences=== {{Quote|You brought the kid?|Koresh's opening line in the junior novel|}} [[Joe Schreiber]]'s [[2022]] [[The Mandalorian Season 2 Junior Novel|junior novelization]] of ''The Mandalorian'' Season Two describes Koresh as having a nose ring, in line with the first drafts of "Chapter 9: The Marshal." However, his depiction in the finished episode did not include a nose ring. The novel also presents some of Koresh's lines differently to how they are said in the episode or presented in the subtitles. Additionally, the novelization describes Koresh rising to his feet when shooting the Gamorrean while the episode shows him being seated until the second Gamorrean attacks Djarin.
